Fast Linear Interpolation with Boundary Handling

Source: R/interpolation.R
dot-fast_interp_approx_internal.Rd

Core interpolation algorithm using base::findInterval() and vectorised linear interpolation. Matches stats::approx() with rule = 2 exactly.

Usage

.fast_interp_approx_internal(mat, xout)

Arguments

mat

Numeric 2-column matrix with x (col 1) and y (col 2) values. Rows may be unordered or contain duplicates.

xout

Numeric vector of x-coordinates to interpolate at.

Value

Numeric vector of interpolated y-values.

Details

Internally calls:

  1. .prep_xy() to sort/deduplicate

  2. .interpolate() to perform vectorised interpolation

Edge cases:

  • Empty xout: returns numeric(0)

  • Single row in matrix: returns y[1] repeated

  • xout below min(x): constant extrapolation to y[1]

  • xout above max(x): constant extrapolation to y[n]

Algorithm

  1. Prepare x-y points (sorted, deduplicated)

  2. Use base::findInterval() to locate each output point in x-grid

  3. Categorize points:

    • Below \(min(x)\): use \(y[1]\) (constant)

    • Above \(max(x)\): use \(y[n]\) (constant)

    • Between \(x[i]\) and \(x[i+1]\): linear interpolation

  4. Return interpolated y-values

Examples

# Simple lookup table
mat <- rbind(c(0, 0.05), c(60, 0.6), c(120, 0.6))
xout <- c(0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150)
y_interp <- .fast_interp_approx_internal(mat, xout)
#> Error in .fast_interp_approx_internal(mat, xout): could not find function ".fast_interp_approx_internal"
cbind(xout, y_interp)
#> Error: object 'y_interp' not found
